transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Um… I guess what finally made me come in is that I keep forgetting basic adult things, and it’s not just annoying anymore, it’s actually starting to mess up my life. Like paying bills on time, replying to interview emails, showing up for appointments, even simple errands I said I’d do — I’ll fully mean to do them, and then somehow they just disappear from my brain until there’s a consequence.

And it’s embarrassing because these are things I feel like I should be able to handle, especially having finished college, but lately it feels like I’m constantly dropping the ball. I’ve missed opportunities because I didn’t respond to emails in time, or I realize too late that I forgot something important. It’s gotten to the point where I’m scared I’m going to keep ruining chances for myself if I don’t figure out what’s going on.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

Um… I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I don’t think I’ve been, like, hopeless exactly. I mean, I definitely get frustrated with myself and embarrassed, and sometimes I feel kind of overwhelmed by everything I’m not keeping up with, but I don’t know if I’d call it “down” in the way you mean.

As far as losing interest in things, I don’t think I’ve really noticed that. I still want to do things I enjoy, at least in theory. It’s more like… I don’t know, I get stuck or distracted or things feel hard to start, but I wouldn’t say I’ve stopped caring about them. I guess I’m not sure where the line is between being stressed and actually feeling depressed.
Can you think of a time recently when you felt genuinely happy or took pleasure in something? How often has that happened in the last couple of weeks?

Yeah, I mean… I think so. I’m trying to think of an actual example and not just give a vague answer. I don’t feel like I’m incapable of feeling happy or enjoying things. Like if something funny happens or I’m talking to someone I like, I can laugh and feel normal in that moment.

In the last couple weeks, I’d say it has happened, but I’m not sure how often exactly. It’s not like every day I’m sitting there feeling miserable. It’s more that the good moments kind of come in little bursts, and then I go back to feeling stressed or like I’m behind on something. But I wouldn’t say I’ve had no pleasure in anything. I still can enjoy things when I’m actually doing them, if that makes sense.
Would you say that, most days, you’ve been in a down mood for most of the day?

I don’t think so, no. At least not “most days” and “most of the day.” I’m trying to be careful because I don’t want to understate it if it matters, but when I think of being in a down mood, like feeling sad or low for hours and hours, that’s not really what stands out to me.

I definitely have moments where I feel bad about myself or kind of defeated, especially if I realize I forgot something or I’m behind again, but it feels more tied to whatever just happened. Then it can pass, or I get distracted by something else, or I’m okay for a while. So I wouldn’t describe my whole day as being down most of the time. It’s more like waves of stress or frustration than a constant depressed mood, if that makes sense.
Do you find it hard to focus or stay on task even when you're not feeling stressed or upset about forgetting things?

Yeah, definitely. That’s actually one of the things that makes me feel like it’s not just stress or being upset, because it happens even when I’m in a totally okay mood.

Like, I’ll sit down and genuinely mean to update my resume, or I’ll open a coding practice problem and be like, okay, I’m going to do this one thing. And then a text notification comes in, or I hear someone talking outside, or honestly sometimes it’s not even something external — it’ll just be some random thought like, “Oh, I need to look up that other thing,” or “Wait, did I ever reply to that email?” And before I even realize I’ve switched tracks, I’m doing something completely different.

It’s not always that I’m avoiding it because I feel bad. Sometimes I’m not upset at all. I just get pulled away so easily, and then ten or twenty minutes later I’m like… wait, I was supposed to be working on the resume. It feels like my attention gets hijacked before I notice it happening.
Do you often find yourself starting tasks but having trouble organizing how to finish them, or do you tend to leave things incomplete even if you meant to follow through?

Yeah, that happens a lot. Probably more than I like to admit, honestly.

It’s like I can start something, especially if someone gives me clear steps, and at first I’m like, okay, great, I know what to do. But then somewhere in the middle it kind of falls apart. Like with job applications, I’ll open the form, fill out part of it, maybe even update one section of my resume, and then there’ll be some part where I need to attach something or write a short response or send an email afterward, and I’ll be like, “I’ll come back to that in a minute.” And then it just… sits there. Half-finished. Sometimes for days.

Same thing with volunteer stuff or anything where there are multiple little steps. I might mean to follow through, and I’m not trying to be flaky, but I end up with unsent emails or drafts that are almost done but not actually sent. And then it becomes harder to go back to because now I have to remember where I left off, and it feels messy.

Even cleaning is like that. I’ll start cleaning the apartment and I’ll move a bunch of things around, make piles, take stuff out so I can organize it, and then somehow I end up with the room looking worse than when I started because I never actually put everything away. It’s not that I don’t care about finishing. I really do mean to. I just lose the thread somewhere between starting and actually completing it.
Do you often struggle with planning out how to approach tasks, keeping track of time while you're working, or putting things in order before you start?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that, because I think I’d need you to tell me what “planning out” counts as. Like, I can make a to-do list sometimes, or I can think, okay, first I’ll open the document, then I’ll do this other part, but I don’t know if I’m actually good at it or if I’m just making a list that makes me feel like I have a plan.

With time, I do notice I can sort of lose track while I’m working, but I don’t always know if that’s unusual or just normal. Sometimes I’ll think something is going to take, like, twenty minutes, and then it’s been way longer, but I haven’t paid attention to exactly how often that happens. And with putting things in order before I start, I guess I don’t always do that unless I’m really forced to. I tend to just start somewhere and then figure it out as I go, which sometimes works and sometimes makes it more confusing.

So… yes, maybe? But I don’t want to overstate it. I know I can feel kind of disorganized around tasks, but I’m not sure I’ve thought about it in those exact categories before.
Looking back, did you have similar struggles with staying focused, remembering tasks, or finishing what you started when you were in school or growing up?

Yeah, looking back, it was definitely there when I was a kid. I don’t think I recognized it that way at the time, because I was doing okay academically in a lot of ways, so people would say I was “bright” or “had potential,” but then the comments on report cards or from teachers were always kind of the same.

In elementary school especially, I remember teachers writing things like I needed to slow down and read the directions, because I would rush through assignments and then miss part of what I was supposed to do. Or I’d finish something quickly but realize later I skipped a whole section because I hadn’t really taken in the instructions.

And I was constantly losing worksheets. Like, not just once in a while — I’d put them in my folder or my desk, and then somehow they were gone. My desk was always this disaster, like papers shoved everywhere, old assignments crumpled up, random stuff mixed together, and when the teacher would say, “Take out the worksheet from yesterday,” I’d be digging around forever and panicking because I couldn’t find it.

I also got in trouble for talking out of turn. Not necessarily trying to be rude, I just had something in my head and it would come out before I stopped myself. So yeah, even pretty early on, it was like I could understand the work, but managing the materials, following the full directions, and actually keeping track of assignments was a mess.
Do you often feel restless or find yourself moving around a lot, even when you're trying to stay still?

Yeah. Very often. It’s actually one of the things I notice the most when I’m in situations where I’m supposed to just sit still and be normal-looking.

Like even sitting through an interview or a meeting, I’ll be trying really hard to listen and look calm, but inside my body it feels like there’s this pressure building up. Not pain exactly, but like this uncomfortable buzzing or tightness, like I need to move or shift or do something with my hands. If I don’t, I feel like I’m going to crawl out of my skin.

Movies are like that too, which is annoying because I want to enjoy them. But after a while I’m changing positions, crossing and uncrossing my legs, messing with my sleeves, picking at something, checking my bag, anything just to have some kind of movement. And if I’m somewhere where I really can’t get up, I feel trapped, like I’m using a ton of effort just to stay seated.

It’s not always that I literally stand up and pace, though sometimes I really want to. A lot of the time it’s smaller stuff, like shifting around constantly or needing to keep my hands busy. But the feeling underneath is pretty strong. It’s like my body is yelling at me to do something even when my brain is trying to stay put.

When you were growing up, did you often act without thinking or have trouble waiting your turn, like blurting out answers before being called on or rushing into things without considering the consequences?

Yeah, I think so, especially with blurting things out. Not always in the obvious way of, like, standing up and shouting answers, but in conversations I would jump in before the other person was actually finished. I’d hear the beginning of what they were saying and my brain would go, “Oh, I know where this is going,” and then I’d answer or respond before they got to the actual question.

And then sometimes I’d realize I had answered the wrong thing, because they weren’t going where I thought they were going at all. Or I’d notice from their face that I had cut them off, and then I’d feel embarrassed and try to backtrack, like, “Sorry, go ahead,” but by then I’d already interrupted the flow.

It happened in interviews too, or more formal situations, which is especially frustrating because I’m trying to make a good impression. I’ll think I’m being engaged or quick, but really I’m jumping ahead and responding too soon. So yes, that part definitely fits for me — acting before I’ve really waited long enough to hear the whole thing.
Have you ever experienced periods where your mood was extremely up and down — like feeling unusually energetic or irritable for days at a time, followed by feeling really low or hopeless?

I don’t think so, not in that kind of clear “for days I’m a totally different person” way. I mean, my mood can definitely go up and down during the day depending on what’s happening, or I can get really frustrated with myself, but I wouldn’t say I’ve had periods where I’m unusually energized for days and then later really hopeless in a dramatic cycle like that.

I’m trying to think if there’s anything that would count, because sometimes it’s hard to know what’s normal stress versus something more. But no, I haven’t really noticed distinct stretches like that. It’s more moment-to-moment for me, not days of being extremely up or extremely low.

I don’t think so, not in that kind of clear “for days I’m a totally different person” way. I mean, my mood can definitely go up and down during the day depending on what’s happening, or I can get really frustrated with myself, but I wouldn’t say I’ve had periods where I’m unusually energized for days and then later really hopeless in a dramatic cycle like that.

I’m trying to think if there’s anything that would count, because sometimes it’s hard to know what’s normal stress versus something more. But no, I haven’t really noticed distinct stretches like that. It’s more moment-to-moment for me, not days of being extremely up or extremely low.
